authoredNote: Written AFTER the fix, and honestly labelled: the RULE is the Svelte 5 language's — `<svelte:component this={X}>` and `<svelte:element this={X}>` each name a dynamic component reference, so a name written at N sites is N references — plus the corpus measurement quoted in the fixture header. The line pins were read off the post-fix run and each checked against the fixture's own text: `Widget` is written on 25, 26, 27 and 33; `Panel` on 30.
rationale: A lossy PROJECTION, not a wrong edge, which is why no gate saw it. The dynamic-target map was `Map<name, line>`, so a name written twice published one edge at the second line and the first site was unrecoverable from the payload. Measured over the 6,439-file corpus: 125 bare-identifier `this={X}` sites in 73 files, 11 of which write one name at more than one site, 36 sites collapsed. `line_number` keeps the LAST site (33 for `Widget`, not 25) so no shared payload baseline moves; the whole set travels in `metadata.dynamicTargetLines`.

forbidRelationships.comment: `line_number` keeps the LAST site, so an edge at the FIRST site cannot appear. This row is what makes that a pinned property rather than an accident: a change that moved `line_number` to the first site would look like an improvement and would break every consumer that reads it.
same — the middle sites are recorded, never claimed as the edge's line
there is no site on 31; a wrong line would be a past-the-tag claim
